bull_case: Customers commit to multi-generation custom accelerators, large non-cancellable RPO and expanding VCF contracts because the products improve performance per watt and are deeply embedded in infrastructure. Gross margin expansion indicates strong willingness to pay.
bear_case: Direct customer ROI and payback are undisclosed. Top-customer concentration is rising, and XPV backstop/customer-note structures mean some future AI demand is partially finance-enabled. A slowdown could expose weaker unit economics than headline margins imply.
thesis: Product-market evidence is strong enough for Growth eligibility but not pristine. Multi-generation design wins, non-terminable contracts and 69% gross margin support willingness to pay and retention proxies. Direct customer ROI/payback is missing, while XPV financing keeps unit economics below the 75 anchor.

evidence.claim: OpenAI and Broadcom said early Jalapeño testing showed better performance per watt than the then-current state of the art, and described a multi-generation deployment plan.
RPO was approximately $179.2B, includes a long-term custom AI accelerator contract, and approximately 25% was expected to be recognized over the next 12 months.

Infrastructure software growth was driven by strong VCF demand and additional license revenue on contracts where customers do not have termination rights; by Q3 the majority of new software contracts no longer had termination-for-convenience provisions.
Q3 FY2026 gross margin was 69% versus 67% a year earlier while revenue rose 86%; 9M gross margin was also 69% versus 68%.

One semiconductor distributor represented 50% of Q3 revenue and top-five end customers about 55%, up from 32% and about 40% respectively a year earlier, showing rapid expansion with a concentrated customer set.

AI XPV carries a maximum $29B lease backstop and the customer may under conditions issue up to $42B of convertible promissory notes to Broadcom; no notes had been issued and no backstop payments made at quarter end.

counterevidence: No disclosed customer-level ROI, payback period, NRR, GRR or churn series exists for the custom-AI programs.
Rising customer concentration can masquerade as retention/wallet-share improvement while increasing bargaining power.
XPV financing means headline demand cannot be treated as entirely unassisted customer demand.
Early performance-per-watt results are company/customer claims rather than independent production benchmarks.
unknowns: Customer-level payback and TCO for custom XPUs and AI networking.
NRR/renewal/churn for VCF under the new contract structure.
Supported-customer revenue share attributable to XPV financing.
falsifiers: Customer-value score falls if independent benchmarks fail to show a material TCO/performance advantage.
Retention score falls if RPO declines while termination rights return or VCF growth stalls.
Unit-economics score falls if funded XPV exposure rises materially while gross margin or OCF conversion deteriorates.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: The veto requires absence of customer value plus subsidy dependence. Multi-generation design wins, non-terminable commitments, 69% gross margin and performance-per-watt evidence refute the required 'no customer value' element. XPV financing remains a unit-economics risk, not this veto by policy.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Concentration is high and the distributor-level >25% watch trigger is met, but a distributor is a channel rather than a disclosed single end customer, and the filings show multiple end customers plus a separate software segment. A single dependency whose loss would irreversibly destroy business economics is not established.

key_kpis.name: RPO and non-cancellable share
key_kpis.threshold: RPO >$150B with majority new software contracts non-terminable

next_checks: Obtain customer TCO/payback or independent accelerator benchmarks.
Track VCF renewal/churn when the new contract cohort matures.
Separate XPV-supported demand from conventionally financed AI demand.

subscores.rationale: Performance-per-watt evidence plus long-term committed purchases place customer value between the 50 'quantitative evidence lacking' and 75 'ROI/pricing confirmed' anchors. 75 is not used because customer-level financial payback/TCO is undisclosed.

Multi-generation AI programs, $179.2B RPO and removal of termination-for-convenience from most new software contracts provide direct commitment and wallet-share expansion proxies consistent with the 75 anchor. 90 is excluded because NRR/churn cohorts are not disclosed.

69% gross margin and strong operating leverage support scale economics, but the $29B backstop and conditional note structure mean some AI growth is finance-assisted. This is stronger than the 50 mixed anchor but below 75.

uncertainties.rationale: No customer-level dollar ROI/payback is disclosed.
Commitments substitute for, but are not identical to, cohort retention data.
XPV can shift customer financing risk back toward Broadcom in a stress case.
